title: Part 3: diskusi akademik, matching & multiple choice
title_target: Listening — who thinks what, and matching items to a list
goal: Mengikuti diskusi tiga suara tanpa kehilangan jejak siapa berpendapat apa, mengerjakan soal matching A–F tanpa terkecoh kata yang sama, dan memilih opsi MCQ berdasarkan makna yang diparafrase, bukan kata yang kebetulan terdengar.
bekal: menandai kepemilikan pendapat lewat frasa seperti honestly, I don't think that was it, that's fair
menghubungkan enam item dengan enam opsi yang hanya boleh dipakai sekali
mengenali opsi yang disebut lalu ditolak dalam soal pilih-dua

sections.title: Part 3: yang dinilai bukan topiknya, tapi siapa bilang apa

blocks.text: Part 3 adalah **diskusi akademik**: dua mahasiswa, sering ditambah seorang tutor, membahas tugas, proyek penelitian, laporan lapangan, atau presentasi yang akan datang. Sepuluh soal, biasanya campuran **multiple choice** dan **matching**, kadang ditambah *flow-chart completion*. Ini bagian tersulit di Listening untuk sebagian besar peserta, dan alasannya bukan kosakata.

Alasannya adalah **kepemilikan pendapat**. Di Part 1 dan Part 2, informasi hanya perlu didengar. Di Part 3, informasi yang sama bisa diucapkan tiga kali oleh tiga orang dengan sikap yang berbeda, dan soalnya menanyakan sikap siapa. *Josh bilang X. Mina bilang X itu bukan masalahnya. Tutor setuju dengan Mina.* Kalau kamu hanya menangkap kata X, kamu akan menjawab dengan pendapat orang yang salah — dan pengecoh di Part 3 memang dibangun persis seperti itu.

Tambahan kesulitan: pembicara Part 3 **berubah pikiran**. Mereka mengusulkan sesuatu, dibantah, lalu menyerah (*…All right. Yes. That's fair.*). Yang dinilai selalu posisi **terakhir**, bukan yang pertama.

blocks.title: Cara memakai unit ini
items: Audionya ada di menu **Simulasi**, diputar sekali seperti tes asli. Buku ini melatih bagian yang menentukan nilai sebelum audio menyala: membaca soal, memprediksi, dan mengenali pengecoh.

Urutannya: (1) baca **sepuluh soal** di Latihan; (2) untuk soal MCQ, lingkari kata yang membedakan tiga opsi; (3) untuk soal matching, **parafrase dulu keenam opsi A–F dengan kata-katamu sendiri** — kalau kamu belum paham opsinya sebelum audio menyala, kamu tidak akan sempat memahaminya sesudahnya; (4) baru baca transkrip **satu kali, tanpa mengulang**.
Saat membaca transkrip, tulis inisial pembicara (D, M, J) di sebelah tiap jawaban yang kamu isi. Kebiasaan kecil ini yang membedakan 6 dari 9 di Part 3.

blocks.text: Satu jebakan khas Part 3: **tutor mengulang pendapat mahasiswa dengan kata yang lebih akademik**. Mahasiswa bilang *two hundred psychology students isn't two hundred students*; tutor menerjemahkannya jadi *a big sample of the wrong people is still the wrong people*. Kalau soal memakai kata *representative*, sumbernya bisa kalimat siapa pun dari keduanya — tapi kalau soal bertanya *what does Mina say*, hanya kalimat Mina yang berlaku.

sections.title: Matching: enam item, enam opsi, sekali pakai

blocks.text: Soal matching Part 3 memberi daftar item (metode, bab, tempat, orang) dan daftar opsi berhuruf A–F atau A–H, biasanya berisi pendapat atau nasib: *akan dipakai sebagai sumber utama, gagal tahun lalu, butuh izin, hanya kalau sempat*. Kesulitannya bukan mendengar — item disebut **berurutan**, satu per satu, rapi. Kesulitannya adalah opsi: enam kalimat abstrak yang harus sudah ada di kepalamu.

items: **Parafrase keenam opsi sebelum audio.** Ubah *It would take too long to analyse* jadi tiga kata milikmu sendiri: *ribet diolah*. Opsi yang belum kamu cerna adalah opsi yang tidak akan kamu kenali saat lewat.

**Perhatikan kata pembeda antaropsi.** Sering ada dua opsi yang mirip: *hard to collect* vs *hard to analyse*, *tutor menyarankan* vs *tutor menyediakan*. Penulis soal menaruh keduanya justru karena bedanya tipis.
**Coret opsi yang sudah terpakai.** Kalau instruksinya *use each letter once only*, tiap coretan mempersempit sisanya. Dua soal terakhir sering terjawab dengan eliminasi, bukan dengan pendengaran.
**Jangan menjawab dari satu kata yang sama.** Mendengar *time* tidak berarti opsi *takes too long*. Jawabannya ada di seluruh kalimat, dan hampir selalu diparafrase.

**Kalau satu item lewat, kosongkan dan lanjut.** Item berurutan — berhenti di item 7 berarti kehilangan 8. Isi yang kosong di akhir dengan huruf yang belum terpakai; peluangnya jauh lebih baik daripada nol.

blocks.title: MCQ Part 3 dan soal 'pilih DUA'
items: MCQ Part 3 sering menanyakan **pendapat**, bukan fakta: *What does Mina say about…* · *What do the students agree about…* · *What does the tutor advise them to do first?* Baca kata kerja di batang soal: *say*, *agree*, *advise*, *decide* menuntut hal yang berbeda-beda.
*What do they AGREE?* berarti jawabannya harus disetujui **kedua** pembicara — satu suara saja tidak cukup, sekeras apa pun.

*What does the tutor advise them to do FIRST?* menuntut urutan. Beberapa saran akan disebut; yang dicari yang paling awal, ditandai *before anything else*, *everything waits on it*, *get that in this week*.

Soal pilih-dua (*Which TWO…*, lima opsi A–E) dinilai dua angka dan urutannya bebas, tapi setengah benar bernilai nol. Di unit ini bentuk itu ditulis sebagai satu item berisi tiga pasangan, supaya bisa dikoreksi otomatis — keterampilannya sama: dua hal harus dipegang bersamaan.

blocks.text: Tiga potongan dari diskusi lain (Amy, Ben, dan tutor mereka membahas laporan kerja lapangan). Perhatikan bahwa di ketiganya, kata yang sama dengan opsi salah diucapkan lebih dulu.

blocks.text: Baris ketiga adalah bentuk pengecoh khas Part 3: **pengulangan bukan kepemilikan**. Orang yang paling sering menyebut sebuah kata biasanya orang yang sedang membantahnya. Yang mengusulkan justru mengucapkannya sekali, pelan, dalam bentuk pertanyaan.
Berhenti di sini. **Baca dulu sepuluh soal di bagian Latihan** dan parafrase keenam opsi di bawah dengan kata-katamu sendiri. Baru setelah itu baca transkrip **satu kali, tanpa mengulang**.

blocks.title: Opsi untuk soal 5–10 — tiap huruf dipakai satu kali
items: **A** It will be the project's main source of data.
**B** It produced disappointing results in a previous project.
**C** It would take the students too long to analyse.
**D** The tutor offers to arrange access to it.
**E** It needs approval that has not yet been given.
**F** They will use it only if there is time at the end.

blocks.title: Two students discuss a research project with their tutor

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Right, Mina, Josh — you asked for twenty minutes on the sleep project. Where have you got to?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: We've got a question, more or less. Something like: does the amount of sleep students get in the week before an exam affect their grade?

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: More or less isn't going to survive ten weeks. Before we talk about method, let me say something about the question itself, because that's where most groups lose marks. Originality is not what we are marking at this level — plenty of perfectly good projects repeat something that has been done before, and I would rather you repeated something well. What the question does have to be is narrow enough to answer in ten weeks, and worded so that the answer can be measured. Affect their grade is not measurable. Which grade? Measured how?

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Their mark in one exam, then. In one module we can name.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Better. Now — last term's project. I marked it. What went wrong?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: We started too late, mainly. We were still writing the questionnaire in week five.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Honestly, Josh, I don't think that was it. We had six weeks of collection, which was plenty, and we got two hundred responses — a hundred and eighty, once you take out the blank ones. Still plenty. The problem was who they were. Every single person who filled it in was on our course, because we put the link in our own group chat and nowhere else. Two hundred psychology students is not two hundred students.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: …All right. Yes. That's fair.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: It's more than fair; it's the reason the mark wasn't higher. A big sample of the wrong people is still the wrong people. So this time: sampling first, everything else second.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Can I say something about the literature before we get to method?

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Go on.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: I've read about fifteen studies now. They don't actually disagree about the number — everyone lands on seven to nine hours, so that argument is settled. What bothers me is the measuring. Almost all of them simply ask people how well they slept last night, and people are hopeless at that. I would swear I had four hours, and my flatmate says I was snoring by ten.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: That's a real criticism, and it happens to be one your project could answer. Which brings us to method. What are you considering?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: We've got a list of six things, and we can't do six.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Read them out.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Online questionnaire first.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: That one isn't negotiable. It's the only instrument two hundred people will actually complete, so everything else hangs off it. It has to carry the project.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Agreed. Next.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Sleep diaries. A week of them, written up each morning.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: I wanted those, and then I did the arithmetic last night. Seven entries times two hundred people, hand-written, free text, and the two of us coding every line by hand — we would still be sitting there in June. Collecting them is easy. It's what comes afterwards that kills us.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Which is the right reason to drop something, by the way. Not because it's hard to get, but because you cannot process it. Third?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Wearable trackers. Wrist monitors. Which we obviously can't afford.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: You don't have to afford them. Sports Science have about thirty sitting in a drawer, and they have been asking for somebody to use them. I'll email Priya this afternoon and put your names on the list.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Seriously? That changes everything.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Fourth was a focus group.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Josh.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: We ran one for the stress project last term. Twenty minutes of six people agreeing with each other and one person doing all the talking. We transcribed the whole thing and used a single quotation. I am not doing that again.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: …I can't argue with that.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Fifth?

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: An overnight laboratory session. Proper equipment, in the sleep lab downstairs.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Stop there. Anything that keeps a participant in a building overnight needs its own ethics application, separate from your main one, and that committee sits twice a term. You haven't submitted the main form yet, have you?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Then it is out, for this project at least. Last one?

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: University attendance records. The registry can give them to us anonymised — how many lectures people actually turned up to.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: I like it, but it's extra.

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Keep it on the list as something you do in week eight, if week eight is kind to you. Don't build the project on it.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: So what do we do first? Pilot the questionnaire?

lines.speaker: Dr Reid
lines.text: Before anything else, the ethics form. Everything waits on it — you cannot pilot, you cannot recruit, you cannot borrow a single wrist monitor until it has been approved. Get it in this week. Then pilot the questionnaire on ten people, then come back to me.

lines.speaker: Josh
lines.text: Right. Ethics form. Today.

Josh mengusulkan opsi B (*We started too late, mainly*), Mina membatalkannya (*Honestly, Josh, I don't think that was it… The problem was who they were*), dan Josh menyerah (*…All right. Yes. That's fair*). Kata kunci di batang soal adalah **finally agree** — posisi terakhir, bukan yang pertama. Opsi A dibunuh angka: *two hundred responses — a hundred and eighty… Still plenty.* Angka yang diralat itu justru dipasang supaya kamu mengira datanya kurang.
A

*Originality is not what we are marking at this level… What the question does have to be is narrow enough to answer in ten weeks, and worded so that the answer can be measured.* Kata *original* diucapkan lebih dulu dan paling menonjol — lalu ditolak. Dua opsi lain memuat *original*, jadi menolak satu kata itu langsung menyisakan satu pasangan.
B

*Almost all of them simply ask people how well they slept last night, and people are hopeless at that.* Opsi A dibalik secara eksplisit di kalimat sebelumnya (*They don't actually disagree about the number… that argument is settled*). Opsi C tidak pernah dibahas Mina — ukuran sampel adalah masalah proyek MEREKA, bukan masalah studi yang dia baca.
A

*Before anything else, the ethics form. Everything waits on it… Get it in this week. Then pilot the questionnaire on ten people.* Batang soal menuntut urutan, dan *before anything else* menjawabnya. Opsi B disebut dua kali — sekali oleh Mina sebagai usul (*So what do we do first? Pilot the questionnaire?*) dan sekali oleh tutor sebagai langkah KEDUA. Opsi C sudah dikerjakan tutornya sendiri.
A

Kuesioner: *It's the only instrument two hundred people will actually complete, so everything else hangs off it. It has to carry the project.* Parafrase opsi A (*main source of data*) tanpa satu kata pun yang sama. Inilah alasan opsi harus kamu cerna sebelum audio.
C

Buku harian tidur: *the two of us coding every line by hand — we would still be sitting there in June. Collecting them is easy. It's what comes afterwards that kills us.* Kalimat terakhir memisahkan opsi C dari opsi yang mirip (*hard to collect*), dan tutornya menegaskan pembedaan itu: *Not because it's hard to get, but because you cannot process it.*
D

Wrist monitor: *Sports Science have about thirty sitting in a drawer… I'll email Priya this afternoon and put your names on the list.* Kata *arrange* tidak pernah diucapkan. Pengecohnya ada di soal 10: registry juga *can give them to us*, dan banyak peserta memasang D di sana.
B

Focus group: *We ran one for the stress project last term. Twenty minutes of six people agreeing with each other… We transcribed the whole thing and used a single quotation.* Hasil mengecewakan di proyek sebelumnya, persis opsi B. Perhatikan Mina tidak setuju pada awalnya lalu menyerah (*I can't argue with that*) — sikap kelompok yang berlaku adalah yang terakhir.
E

Sesi laboratorium: *needs its own ethics application, separate from your main one… You haven't submitted the main form yet, have you? — Not yet.* Opsi C menggoda karena kata *overnight* terdengar makan waktu, tapi yang menghentikannya adalah izin, bukan durasi.
F

Data kehadiran: *Keep it on the list as something you do in week eight, if week eight is kind to you. Don't build the project on it.* Persis opsi F. Kalimat Mina sebelumnya (*I like it, but it's extra*) sudah memberi arah yang sama.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari diskusi ini
items: Tiga soal (1, 2, 3) dimenangkan oleh **kalimat penolak**, bukan oleh kata kunci: *I don't think that was it* · *Originality is not what we are marking* · *They don't actually disagree about the number*. Kalau kamu hanya menunggu kata dari opsi muncul di audio, kamu akan memilih opsi yang ditolak setiap kali — karena opsi yang ditolak memang selalu diucapkan lebih dulu.

Soal matching di sini berjalan **berurutan dan rapi**: enam metode dibacakan satu per satu oleh Josh. Yang tidak rapi adalah opsinya. Investasikan seluruh jeda persiapanmu untuk memahami A–F, bukan untuk membaca daftar metodenya — daftar itu akan dibacakan untukmu.

Perhatikan pola *saya usul → dibantah → saya menyerah* yang muncul dua kali (Josh soal keterlambatan, Mina soal focus group). Di Part 3, orang berubah pikiran, dan jawabannya selalu ada di posisi terakhir. Kalau kamu menjawab sebelum pertukaran itu selesai, kamu menjawab pendapat yang sudah dicabut.
